title: Fivefold
tagline: Five in a row. Read the threats before they read you.
teaser: The oldest race on a grid: get five stones in a line before your opponent does. Fivefold pits you against a 1994 Berkeley mind that hunts in hidden combinations — and lets you switch on its thoughts to learn how it plays.

manPage.synopsis: fivefold — place stones in turn; the first to make five in a row wins, against a 1994 mind that hunts combinations.
manPage.description: Ralph Campbell's five-in-a-row program reached Berkeley's games in 1994. It thinks in frames, every run of five points on the board, and hunts for combinations of frames that force a win; it was made for robot tournaments, where a referee program pits one player against another. Fivefold keeps its mind, move for move, and lets you watch it think.

howToPlay: Take turns placing pieces where the lines cross; five in an unbroken line — across, down or on a slant — wins.
Answer every four at once, and stop an open three before it becomes an open four.
Read the board (T) draws the fours and open threes for you in practice, puzzles and two-player games.
